parts.text:
The value of the enthalpy change for process 1 can be calculated using the values of **five** other enthalpy changes which are **not** referred to in Fig. 2.1.

$$\text{process 1:} \quad \text{Ca(s)} + \text{F}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(g)} + 2\text{F}^-\text{(g)}$$

Identify these **five** other enthalpy changes, using either names or symbols.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
At $298\text{ K}$, the Gibbs free energy change, $\Delta G$, for the solution of compound **T** is $+6.00\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

The enthalpy change of solution, $\Delta H_{\text{sol}}$, of compound **T** is $+30.0\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ at $298\text{ K}$.

Calculate the value of the entropy change, $\Delta S$, for the solution of compound **T** at $298\text{ K}$.
